sentiment.label: neutral
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è neutrale oggi, con un indice VIX in aumento del 2.94% a 15.77, ma ancora al di sotto della soglia di panico di 20. L'S&P 500 registra un aumento dello 0.22% a 7580.06. Il DXY si rafforza dello 0.13% a 99.04, segnalando un impatto leggermente negativo sui risk asset. Il prezzo del petrolio (Brent) aumenta del 2.29% a $94.16, influenzato dalle tensioni geopolitiche. Gli articoli di BlackRock Investment Institute e Goldman Sachs Insights segnalano cautela sui mercati, con un focus su energia e inflazione.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is neutral today, with the VIX index up 2.94% to 15.77, still below the panic threshold of 20. The S&P 500 gains 0.22% to 7580.06. The DXY strengthens 0.13% to 99.04, indicating a slightly negative impact on risk assets. Oil prices (Brent) rise 2.29% to $94.16, driven by geopolitical tensions. BlackRock Investment Institute and Goldman Sachs Insights articles express caution on markets, focusing on energy and inflation.

Il Nikkei giapponese sale dello 0.91% a 66,934, mentre lo Shanghai cinese scende dello 0.27% a 4057.74. Il TLT bond USA 20Y registra un aumento dello 0.02% a 85.76. L'oro scende dello 0.45% a $4539.80/oz. Gli analisti di BlackRock e Goldman Sachs segnalano un contesto macroeconomico complesso, con un'attenzione particolare alle dinamiche energetiche e ai trend inflazionistici.
market_impact_summary.en: The stock market shows a cautious opening in Europe, with the STOXX 600 down 0.02% to 62.90. Japan's Nikkei rises 0.91% to 66,934, while Shanghai falls 0.27% to 4057.74. The US 20Y TLT bond gains 0.02% to 85.76. Gold prices decline 0.45% to $4539.80/oz. BlackRock and Goldman Sachs analysts highlight a complex macroeconomic environment, with a focus on energy dynamics and inflation trends.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.9%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.3%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Passiamo ai mercati occidentali. L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.2%, il VIX è in aumento del 2.9%, segnale di maggiore incertezza. Il Dollar Index è in rialzo dello 0.1%, mentre l'euro/dollaro è in calo dello 0.02% a 1.16 L'oro è sceso dello 0.45% a $4539.8/oz. Il petrolio brent è in rialzo del 2.3% a $94.16 I rendimenti dei titoli di stato americani sono pressoché stabili, con il decennale US 10Y Yield in calo dello 0.04% al 4.45%. Il TLT Bond USA 20Y è in rialzo dello 0.02%.

Sul fronte geopolitico, l'Iran si appresta a subire una shock inflazionistico inferiore a quello del 2022 Inoltre, l'attenzione si concentra sulla sicurezza delle infrastrutture sottomarine critiche della NATO.

Infine, sul fronte macro, nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
  Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantamila dollari, ma registra una lieve flessione dell'uno virgola cinquantasei percento, portandosi a settantaduemila seicentosessantatre dollari. 
  I flussi ETF mostrano un deflusso significativo di centoventicinque virgola tre milioni di dollari. 
  Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dichiarazioni di Michael Saylor, che ha accennato a un possibile acquisto di BTC.

  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum scende dell'uno virgola ottantasei percento a mille novecento ottantadue dollari, mentre Solana perde l'uno virgola ottantasei percento a ottantuno virgola zero uno dollari. 
  BNB registra una flessione del due virgola cinquantasei percento, portandosi a settecentouno virgola ventisette dollari.

  Il Fear & Greed Index si attesta a ventinove, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.9%, while Shanghai fell 0.3%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. Let's pivot to the Western markets. The S&P 500 closed up 0.2%, while the VIX rose 2.9%, a signal of increased uncertainty. The Dollar Index is up 0.1%, while the euro/dollar is down 0.02% to 1.16 Gold fell 0.45% to $4539.8/oz. Brent oil is up 2.3% to $94.16 US Treasury yields are essentially flat, with the 10-year US 10Y Yield down 0.04% to 4.45%. The TLT Bond USA 20Y is up 0.02%. On the geopolitical front, Iran is set to experience a lower inflationary shock than in 2022 Additionally, attention is focused on the security of NATO's critical underwater infrastructure. Finally, on the macro front, there are no significant economic data releases today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above seventy thousand dollars but registers a slight decline of 1.56%, bringing it to $72,663 ETF flows show a significant outflow of $125.3 million. This movement may be influenced by recent statements from Michael Saylor, who hinted at a possible purchase of BTC. Among altcoins, Ethereum falls 1.86% to $1,982, while Solana loses 1.86% to $81.01 BNB records a decline of 2.56%, bringing it to $701.27 The Fear & Greed Index stands at 29, in the Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors. No macro data in the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the complete articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Deterring Russia Beneath the Waves: Securing NATO’s Critical Undersea Infrastructure
articles.snippet: What would happen if you woke up one morning and the internet was gone — not from a software glitch, but because someone had simply cut the wire?Threats to critical undersea infrastructure are rapidly escalating. In 2023, the Balticonnector pipeline and several Baltic data cables were damaged. A year later, four Red Sea cables were cut, disrupting a quarter of data traffic between Asia and Europe, with further incidents across the Baltic. In total, between January 2024 and July 2025, roughly 44 incidents of cable damage were recorded. Not all were deliberate, but Russia’s activity has grown brazen. articles.title: The Iran War’s First 90 Days Upended Energy Markets
articles.snippet: The Iran war suddenly turned what had started as a year of oversupply in global oil and LNG markets into the worst oil and gas supply disruption in history. Three months after the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28, the world has already lost 1 billion barrels of crude oil supply, oil and gas prices have found a new, much higher floor, and whipsaw with violent volatility nearly every day, trade routes have shifted, and tanker rates have spiked. Actual supply shortages are emerging in Asia, while global crude and fuel inventories…

articles.title: Disaster of Brexit is a warning against simple solutions to hard problems | Richard Partington
articles.snippet: Alan Milburn says youth unemployment has no quick fixes – an idea with an important lesson for those thinking about how to rejoin the EU Mainstream politicians are rarely direct. It is part of the reason why their populist counterparts thrive: they say it like it is. No nonsense. Let’s get things done. But last week Alan Milburn had a frank rebuttal: “Everybody goes for the bloody easy solution, don’t they? You can’t just go for the easy solution, OK? There are no easy solutions, guys. None. They’re all hard.” Speaking at the launch of his review into Britain’s youth worklessness crisis , the former Labour cabinet minister was arguing that one tax U-turn could not fix a problem decades in the making. Continue reading...
